text:
incident-bot: PAGER: SRE oncall triggered for GPU capacity exhaustion in cluster-inference-eu-west-1 :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Alerts: queue_length > 500 for model-inf-prod, token throttling observed, latency spike > 2.5s. Paging oncall: @alice.k

alice.k: I'm up. joining.

jon.p: seeing autoscaler errors: "unable to provision nodes: RunInstances AccessDenied" in controller-manager logs. suspect launch template/IAM change.

marta.r: confirming — last change to nodegroup LT was 2 hours ago from infra-rollout. Could be a version drift.

alice.k: can someone paste the autoscaler log lines? I have the alert graph open.

jon.p: log snippets:
```
E0321 14:23:45 autoscaler.go:312] Scale-up failed: error creating nodegroup: InvalidLaunchTemplateSpecification: Launch template version 1 is deprecated for this ASG
caused by: AccessDenied when calling RunInstances: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-node-role is not authorized to perform: ec2:RunInstances
```

alice.k: hmm AccessDenied + LT version mismatch. Maybe launch template pinned to specific SG or a changed AMI. If RunInstances is denied, IAM role for autoscaler or instance profile changed.

kevin.t: checking infra logs — we did a small service account migration at 13:40. Could be related.

marta.r: customer impact: model-inf-prod queue is backlogged; API error rate up ~4% and retries causing higher cost. customers affected: internal test tenants + some prod customers. Need mitigation ASAP.

alice.k: immediate mitigation plan:
1) manually increase ASG desired to add a non-gpu fallback pool? we need GPUs so fallback not ideal.
2) launch a temporary GPU node manually using ops account (bypass autoscaler) to drain queue.
3) revert the service account IAM change if it's root cause.

eng-oncall: I can manually launch a spot instance in the GPU pool with same launch template but explicit version. Command:
```
aws ec2 run-instances --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd --version 2 --instance-type p4d.24xlarge --count 1
```

jon.p: trying run-instances with the node role creds returns AccessDenied as well. ops account should work. eng-oncall, can you try?

eng-oncall: launching now with ops creds, started instance i-0f1234. kubelet registered in ~90s, taint mismatch detected though: node has taint gpu=true:NoSchedule but pods expect accelerator=nvidia. the daemonSet uses different label.

alice.k: quick fix: apply toleration to the model-inf-prod daemonset so it can schedule, will only be temporary. Patch:
```
kubectl -n prod patch deployment model-inf-prod --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
```

kevin.t: done. pods starting on new node, queue draining.

marta.r: customer-facing note: informing SRE-CS to open a short incident notification: some requests delayed; mitigation in progress. ETA to normal ~15-25m.

sre-lead: we need root cause timeline: autoscaler IAM role change at 13:40 -> subsequent autoscaler failures -> queue growth. Postmortem candidate.

alice.k: handoff in 30m to @jon.p for stabilization and RC. I'm going offline for PM but will monitor. leaving notes:
- ops manual instance used as stopgap
- revert IAM change or restore RunInstances permission to autoscaler role
- reconcile launch template versions across ASG and nodegroups

jon.p: taking over. will coordinate with infra team to roll a corrected launch template and run a controlled rolling replace.

eng-oncall: instance i-0f1234 draining, scaling back desired capacity to pre-incident after job drain.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 — partial service degradation but user-visible impact limited and mitigated :white_check_mark:

jon.p: will create a follow-up ticket with owner tags: infra/launch-templates, iam/audit, oncall/sre. tagging marta for customer comms.

marta.r: thanks — I'll draft the customer message and timeline. follow-up meeting in 45m.

alice.k: signed off handoff — good catch everyone :thumbsup:
